summary: Adds a new SKILL.md, adversarial-review-2, a systematic red-team review skill. It runs five stages: intake with an overkill check, a one-page charter of ranked harm categories, three parallel fresh-eyes adversary subagents with distinct lenses and a fixed finding format, main-agent verification with dedup, seam sweep, outcome-based severity rubric and strict total ranking, a fixed-section report, then a retest loop after fixes. Includes gotchas and a worked example finding.

claims.text: Description positions skill as distinct from adversarial-review (conversational) and debate-review (neutral judge), and excludes routine diff review.
Claims NIST, OWASP, and Microsoft's 100-product retrospective converge on discipline-over-cleverness with five elements.
Charter written to adversarial-review-2/charter.md with four sections; review stops without harm categories.
Three adversaries spawned in parallel, each receiving only brief, artifact, and charter, never conversation history.
Severity graded by outcome via four-row rubric, then ranked in strict total order with no ties.
Report has six fixed sections; retest re-runs each Confirmed finding's original scenario after fixes.

risks.note: Literature citations (NIST, OWASP, Microsoft) named without links or titles; readers cannot check the claimed convergence.
'Literature's most-cited failure mode' asserted without source.
Example finding presented as verbatim from a real run; no run or file is referenced.
Overkill check says 'four subagents' but Stage 2 spawns three; count inconsistent.

least_confident: I could not check whether the cited red-teaming literature (NIST, OWASP, Microsoft retrospective) actually states the five discipline elements attributed to it.
